name: Ur-Nammu Foundation Cone and Cuneiform Cylinder
origin_location: Ur, Southern Mesopotamia (Modern Tell el-Muqayyar, Iraq)
storage_location: Gallery A - Ancient Near East, Case 3
description: A conical terracotta foundation nail inscribed with seventeen lines of archaic Sumerian cuneiform script. Synthetically created for museum collection simulations.
historical_context: Created during the Third Dynasty of Ur to sanctify the foundation deposits of the temple of the moon god Nanna. Foundation cones served as permanent legal and religious dedications.
provenance: Recovered during the 1928-1930 Joint Expedition of the British Museum and University of Pennsylvania; allocated through partition agreements; transferred to registry in 1954.
restoration_notes: Consolidated micro-fractures along base perimeter in 1982 using Paraloid B-72 (3% in acetone). Desalination baths completed in deionized water.

name: Pectoral Collar of Princess Neferure
storage_location: Gallery B - Pharaonic Egypt, Treasury Vitrine
description: An opulent broad collar consisting of eight concentric rows of drop and cylinder beads terminating in chased gold Horus falcon heads. Synthetically generated for museum research cataloging.
historical_context: Associated with the royal court of female Pharaoh Hatshepsut and her daughter Princess Neferure during the 18th Dynasty. Such regalia symbolized cosmic protection.
provenance: Excavated from the Royal Cache vicinity in 1898; acquired by the Lord Mountjoy Collection in 1904; bequeathed to the archival registry in 1968.
restoration_notes: Re-strung in 1999 on synthetic monofilament core mimicking ancient linen cord tension. Surface gold cleaned ultrasonically with mild non-ionic surfactant.

name: Corinthian Bronze Hoplite Helmet of the Peloponnesian War
description: A single-piece hammered bronze helmet with almond-shaped eye slits, distinct nasal bar, and flared neck guard. Displaying active bronze disease stabilization.
historical_context: Standard defensive equipment of heavy Spartan and Athenian infantrymen during the Peloponnesian campaigns. Votive offerings of damaged helmets were common at Olympian shrines.
provenance: Purchased from Munzen & Medaillen AG, Basel, 1972; previously in the collection of Count von Waldburg, Zurich.
restoration_notes: Treated for bronze disease (cuprous chloride) with benzotriazole (BTA) immersion in 2011. Climate-controlled sealed desiccated mount maintaining relative humidity below 35%.

name: Imperial Roman Bust of Emperor Hadrian in Cuirass
description: Over-lifesize marble bust portraying Emperor Hadrian wearing an ornate military cuirass embossed with a gorgoneion (head of Medusa) and heraldic palmettes.
historical_context: Created during Hadrian's principate to project imperial vigilance and philhellenic beard fashion throughout Roman administrative complexes.
provenance: Discovered in the Canopus area of Villa Adriana during 1902 Italian state clearances; transferred through inter-institutional treaty in 1932.
restoration_notes: Laser ablation cleaning carried out in 2016 to remove 18th-century animal-glue varnish residues without disturbing original mineral patina.

name: Tang Dynasty Sancai Glazed Caparisoned Warhorse
medium_materials: Sancai lead glaze (copper green, iron amber, cream)
storage_location: Gallery D - East Asian Arts, Central Island
description: A magnificent earthenware burial steed modeled in full stride with arched neck, docked tail, and draped saddle blanket coated in running sancai dripped glazes.
historical_context: Mingqi (spirit goods) produced during the height of the Silk Road trade under Emperor Xuanzong to accompany aristocratic tombs as symbols of martial nobility.
provenance: Acquired at Sotheby's London, June 1985; previously held in the private estate of Sir Arthur Wherry, Gloucestershire.
restoration_notes: Ear and tail joins secured in 1991 with reversible Paraloid B-48. Minor glaze loss along left flank retouched using water-based gouache under micro-crystalline wax barrier.

name: Planispheric Brass Astrolabe of al-Sahlani
storage_location: Gallery E - Science in Antiquity, Vault Case 1
description: An exquisitely engraved planispheric brass astrolabe featuring an ornate openwork rete with 28 star pointers, four climate plates, and Kufic astronomical inscriptions.
historical_context: Used by medieval Islamic astronomers and navigators for computing solar elevation, qibla direction toward Mecca, and planetary horoscopes.
provenance: Preserved in the Royal Library of Tehran until 1912; acquired by diplomat Henri de Clisson; bequeathed to the registry in 1978.
restoration_notes: Alidade hinge pin lubricated with high-purity synthetic micro-oil. No abrasive polishes applied; original dark olive patina preserved intact.

name: Obsidian Ceremonial Mirror of the Feathered Serpent Priest
description: A circular disc of black vitreous obsidian polished to a high reflective gloss on both faces, perforated with dual suspension holes at the upper rim.
historical_context: Central instrument in Mesoamerican shamanic rituals representing the smoky mirror of Tezcatlipoca, used by elite priests for underworld scrying and prophecy.
provenance: Recovered during the 1961 Carnegie Institution joint salvage expedition at Kaminaljuyu Mound B; legally transferred to museum custody in 1963.
restoration_notes: Edge chips stabilized with optically clear epoxy. Surface cleaned with high-purity ethanol to eliminate modern wax residues.

name: Champleve Enamel Reliquary Casket of the Holy Cross
alternate_names: Limoges Chasse of the True Relic
origin_location: Limoges, Duchy of Aquitaine, Kingdom of France
description: A house-shaped liturgical reliquary casket decorated with brilliant turquoise, cobalt blue, and vermilion champleve enamel portraying the Crucifixion and saints.
historical_context: Manufactured in Limoges workshops for abbey treasuries to house precious relic fragments associated with pilgrims returning from the Holy Land.
provenance: Held in the treasury of Saint-Martial Abbey, Limoges, until 1791; acquired by Baron Charles de Saint-Germain; donated by family trust in 1950.
restoration_notes: Internal oak core monitored for woodworm with non-destructive X-ray micro-tomography. Enamel borders consolidated with acrylic dispersion Plextol B-500.

name: Florentine Renaissance Walnut Cassone with Gilded Pastiglia
storage_location: Decorative Arts Holding Room 2, Bay C
description: A monumental marriage chest featuring carved acanthus pilasters, raised gilded pastiglia relief scenes of Roman triumphs, and heraldic marital cartouches.
historical_context: Commissioned for patrician marriage processions in 15th-century Florence to transport bridal dowries and furnish the master bedchamber.
provenance: Palazzo Davanzati furnishings, Florence; private collection of Marchese Torrigiani; sold at Christie's Rome, 1988.
restoration_notes: Structural consolidation of base plinth in 2004 following minor wood beetle activity. Anoxic nitrogen pest eradication treatment completed.

name: Muramasa School Katana with Dragon-Engraved Tsuba
description: An extraordinarily sharp curved samurai blade with active gunome-midare hamon temper line, signed tang, and blackened shakudo sword guard inlaid with gold dragons.
historical_context: Crafted by swordsmiths of the Muramasa lineage in Ise during the turbulent Sengoku-Edo transition; renowned in folklore as legendary demon blades.
provenance: Hereditary treasure of the Nabeshima samurai clan; exported under cultural ministry license in 1962; gifted to registry by collector Kenzo Mori in 1994.
restoration_notes: Polished by a certified sword polisher (togishi) using traditional uchigumori waterstones in Kyoto, 2012. Treated periodically with camellia oil (choji).

name: Benin Kingdom Cast Bronze Commemorative Head of an Oba
storage_location: Gallery F - African Royal Traditions, Case 1
description: A hollow cast bronze royal portrait head with tiered coral bead choker reaching to the lower lip, scarification crests above the brow, and circular aperture for carved ivory tusk.
historical_context: Commissioned by an incoming Oba (king) of Benin to sanctify the ancestral altar dedicated to his deceased predecessor, embodying dynastic power.
provenance: Removed from Benin City during the 1897 British Expedition; private collection of General Augustus Pitt-Rivers; acquired at London auction in 1960.
restoration_notes: Dry mechanical dust removal; no chemical strippers applied. Stable dark brown and green cuprite patina verified through non-destructive X-ray fluorescence (XRF).

name: Vellum Folio of the Blue Qur'an with Kufic Gold Chrysography
description: A double-sided parchment folio soaked in royal indigo vegetable dye, inscribed with fifteen horizontal lines of un-vocalized Kufic script in glittering liquid shell gold.
historical_context: Believed to have been created for the Great Mosque of Kairouan under the Fatimid or Abbasid governors, mimicking the imperial purple codices of Byzantine emperors.
provenance: Documented in the 1294 inventory of the Kairouan Mosque library; dispersed in early 20th century; acquired via Drouot Paris in 1982.
restoration_notes: Mounted in a bespoke nitrogen-purged hermetic cassette with UV-filtering borosilicate glass. Monitored strictly at 45% relative humidity and 18 degrees Celsius.

name: Viking Silver Hoard Penannular Thistle Brooch
origin_location: Bay of Skaill, Mainland Orkney Islands, Scotland
storage_location: Gallery H - Viking North Sea World, Case 5
description: A massive penannular silver brooch featuring bulbous thistle-head terminals covered in fine prickly granulation, complete with an exceptionally long swivel cloak pin.
historical_context: Worn by high-status Norse jarls across the Irish Sea and Scottish isles as both functional garment fasteners and portable bullion currency.
provenance: Discovered in 1858 in a stone embankment at Skaill; portion acquired through Scottish antiquities bequest; purchased at Edinburgh sale in 1965.
restoration_notes: Tarnish reduction accomplished with electrolytic bath in 1974. Pin swivel stabilized; protected with microcrystalline wax (Renaissance Wax).

name: Inca Featherwork Ceremonial Tunic of the Sun Priest
description: A sleeveless ceremonial tunic constructed from thousands of iridescent yellow, cyan, and scarlet tropical bird feathers tied individually in overlapping rows to a cotton warp.
historical_context: Exclusively donned by royal Sapa Inca priests during Inti Raymi winter solstice festivals to channel the radiance of the solar deity.
provenance: Preserved in coastal dry gravel caches near Ica; collected by archaeologist Ernst Middendorf in 1885; bequeathed to the registry in 1975.
restoration_notes: Stabilized with silk crepeline backing in 2008. Feathers dusted using gentle ultrasonic vacuum nozzle with HEPA particulate trap.

name: Marine Chronometer No. 12 by John Harrison Apprentice
storage_location: Gallery E - Science in Antiquity, Case 8
description: A gimbaled marine chronometer with bi-metallic temperature compensation curb, detent escapement, winding indicator, and original brass-bound three-tier mahogany box.
historical_context: Instruments of this design allowed British Royal Navy navigators to determine true longitude at sea, transforming global maritime trade and cartography.
provenance: Supplied to the Board of Longitude in 1782; issued to HMS Reliance; deaccessioned by Admiralty in 1892; acquired at Christie's London in 1983.
restoration_notes: Cleaned, lubricated, and calibrated by British Horological Institute fellows in 2015. Mainspring tension relieved for static display stability.

name: Hellenistic Tanagra Terracotta Figurine of a Veiled Dancer
description: A graceful terracotta statuette of a young woman wrapped closely in a flowing chiton and himation cloak, captured mid-step with a sun-fan in hand.
historical_context: Tanagra figurines flourished in Hellenistic Greece as domestic luxury decor and grave goods reflecting fashionable aristocratic daily life rather than Olympian deities.
provenance: Excavated from Boeotian necropolis in 1874; collection of Charles Ionides, London; donated to museum collection in 1969.
restoration_notes: Traces of fugitive pigments stabilized with 1% solution of Klucel G in ethanol. Head join checked and reinforced.

name: Byzantine Cloisonne Enamel Medallion of the Archangel Michael
description: A circular gold plaque depicting the Archangel Michael in imperial court loros with vermilion wings, holding a globe and jeweled scepter in vibrant cloisonne cells.
historical_context: Produced in the imperial palace ateliers of the Komnenian dynasty as an adornment for an iconostasis frame or liturgical crown.
provenance: Preserved in the Monastery of Vatopedi on Mount Athos until 1821; collection of Prince Pierre Soltykoff, Paris; acquired in 1974.
restoration_notes: Ultrasonic surface rinse; no modern inpainting applied. Cloison cell adhesion monitored with binocular stereo microscopy.

name: Song Dynasty Ru Ware Celadon Narcissus Basin
origin_location: Qingliangsi Kilns, Baofeng, Henan Province, China
storage_location: Gallery D - East Asian Arts, Imperial Case 1
description: An oval four-legged narcissus basin displaying an ethereal duck-egg sky-blue glaze with delicate ice crackle and five tiny sesame-seed spur marks on the base.
historical_context: Fewer than one hundred complete pieces of Ru ware survive globally; made exclusively during a twenty-year window for Emperor Huizong of the Northern Song.
provenance: Imperial Qing Dynasty collection, Palace of Heavenly Purity; exported via Tianjin in 1924; Sir Percival David associates; bequeathed in 1991.
restoration_notes: In pristine original condition. Never ground or altered. Encapsulated in anti-seismic pendulum mount display vitrine.

name: Gothic Illuminated Book of Hours of Yolande of Valois
alternate_names: Flemish Master of Mary of Burgundy Manuscript
description: A 214-folio illuminated devotional codex containing twenty-four full-page calendar miniatures and intricate trompe-l'oeil floral borders crawling with insects.
historical_context: Custom-crafted for aristocratic contemplation during private daily prayer hours, showcasing the peak of Flemish Gothic naturalism.
provenance: Owned by Yolande of Valois; Duke of Arenberg library until 1952; private Swiss collector; bequeathed to registry in 1962.
restoration_notes: Binding consolidated with calf vellum hinge strips in 1995. Micro-environmental monitoring of iron gall ink corrosion shows zero degradation.

name: Safavid Silk and Metallic Thread Polonaise Falconry Carpet
description: A luxurious tapestry-woven silk pile carpet brocaded with gleaming silver-gilt thread in swirling cloud-band and falconry motifs on pastel green and salmon fields.
historical_context: Commissioned by Shah Abbas the Great at the royal Isfahan workshops to present as lavish diplomatic gifts to Polish, Venetian, and French ambassadors.
provenance: Preserved in the Czartoryski Castle collection, Krakow; private sale in London, 1980.
restoration_notes: Stabilized with custom dyed linen support mesh along frayed edges. Rolled onto an acid-free 30cm diameter archival cylinder.

name: Olmec Jadeite Mask of the Were-Jaguar Deity
description: A magnificent jadeite mask exhibiting the classic Olmec cleft head, almond eyes, and downward-curving feline were-jaguar mouth with drilled earlobes.
historical_context: The Olmec, regarded as the 'mother culture' of Mesoamerica, prized translucent blue jadeite above all gold for funerary and divine rain transformation rites.
provenance: Found near Complex A, La Venta in 1941; collection of Miguel Covarrubias; bequeathed to the registry in 1966.
restoration_notes: Cleaned with non-abrasive distilled water rinses; cinnabar residues left strictly in situ for archaeological record.

name: Renaissance Nuremberg Silver-Gilt Standing Cup (Pokal)
origin_location: Nuremberg, Free Imperial City, Holy Roman Empire
description: An opulent covered standing cup featuring embossed lobe patterns, a cast stem shaped as a draped mythological caryatid, and a finial surmounted by Roman warrior Minerva.
historical_context: Produced in Nuremberg, the goldsmithing capital of Central Europe, as ceremonial guild banquet drinking vessels and civic prestige displays.
provenance: Nuremberg Merchant Guild collection until 1806; Rothschild Collection, Frankfurt; acquired via Sotheby's Zurich, 1977.
restoration_notes: Ultrasonic bath cleaning followed by protective microcrystalline wax coating. No loss of mercury gilding detected.

name: Ancient Roman Cameo Glass Amphora of Bacchic Revels
medium_materials: Opaque white carved cameo glass overlay
description: An exceedingly rare two-handled cameo glass vessel carved in high relief with seven figures of Dionysian satyrs and maenads against a translucent deep cobalt background.
historical_context: Created during the Julio-Claudian dynasty using the gemstone cameo-carving technique applied to blown glass, rivaling the famous Portland Vase in technical mastery.
provenance: Discovered in a Roman tomb near Frascati in 1824; Barberini family collection; acquired through testamentary bequest in 1958.
restoration_notes: Undergoing active consolidation for devitrification stress fractures. Supported with bespoke contoured silicone cradle.

name: Mayan Polychrome Cylinder Vase of the Underworld Ballgame
alternate_names: Classic Maya Codex Style Ceramic Vessel
description: A tall cylindrical ceramic drinking cup painted in codex style depicting the Hero Twins playing the sacred ballgame against the underworld Lords of Xibalba.
historical_context: Used in elite Maya royal feasts for drinking spiced cacao beverages, inscribed along the upper rim with the Primary Standard Sequence hieroglyphic dedicatory formula.
provenance: Recovered during the 1968-1970 University Museum Tikal Project; legal division agreement with Guatemalan government.
restoration_notes: Sherd joins consolidated with cellulose nitrate adhesive; cleaned of calcareous mineral encrustations with 5% EDTA solution.

name: Galilean Refracting Telescope with Tooled Leather Barrel
alternate_names: Early Venetian Spyglass of the Optic Tube
origin_location: Venice / Padua, Republic of Venice, Italy
storage_location: Gallery E - Science in Antiquity, Vitrine 4
description: A single-draw astronomical refracting telescope with plano-convex objective and plano-concave eyepiece lenses housed in an embossed leather-wrapped pine tube.
historical_context: Modeled on the seminal instruments built by Galileo Galilei to confirm the Copernican heliocentric cosmos, tracking Jupiter's satellites and lunar craters.
provenance: Private cabinet of curiosities of Count Francesco Algarotti, Venice; purchased at Christie's London in 1964.
restoration_notes: Lenses cleaned with optical tissue and absolute isopropyl alcohol. Flaking leather binding consolidated with Klucel G in ethanol.

name: Mamluk Enameled and Gilded Mosque Lamp with Throne Verse
storage_location: Islamic Art Wing, Central Chandelier Case
description: A flared glass mosque suspension lamp enameled in vibrant cobalt and cinnabar with Quranic Ayah an-Nur (the Light Verse) and blazons of Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad.
historical_context: Suspended on chains in the grand madrasas and mosques of 14th-century Cairo, serving as physical metaphors for divine illumination.
provenance: Commissioned for the Mosque of Sultan Hasan, Cairo; acquired by French collector Albert Goupil in 1867; purchased by registry in 1970.
restoration_notes: Surface deposits removed using deionized water swabs. Suspension loop handles intact and tested for micro-fractures.

name: Ancient Etruscan Granulated Gold Fibula with Chimaera Motif
storage_location: Gallery A - Classical Mediterranean, Jewelry Safe 2
description: An exquisite leech-shaped gold dress fibula ornamented with microscopic gold granulation beads forming mythical chimaeras, sphinxes, and geometric palmettes.
historical_context: Etruscan goldsmiths achieved unsurpassed mastery of granulation—soldering microscopic gold dust without visible solder—during the 7th-century Orientalizing period.
provenance: Found in the Regolini-Galassi tomb vicinity, Cerveteri in 1888; collection of Count Grigori Stroganoff, Rome; acquired in 1955.
restoration_notes: Ultrasonic bath in mild non-ionic surfactant. Pin spring mechanism structurally sound.

name: Alhambra Nasrid Lusterware Winged Vase of the Gazelles
description: A monumental amphora-shaped jar with large wing-like handles, painted with iridescent metallic luster portraying facing gazelles, arabesque scrollwork, and kufic benedictions.
historical_context: Known as 'Alhambra vases', these monumental ceramics stood in palace niches of the Nasrid kings of Granada as ultimate feats of Moorish luster technology.
provenance: Discovered in the Alhambra subterranean vaults in 1780; collection of the Duke of Osuna, Madrid; acquired in 1973.
restoration_notes: Right wing handle join reinforced with titanium internal pins and epoxy in 1989. Surface salt efflorescence removed.

name: Watt & Boulton Model Indicator and Steam Pressure Gauge
storage_location: Gallery E - Science in Antiquity, Case 14
description: An early mechanical steam engine indicator with brass cylinder, spring-loaded piston, and pencil tracer arm for recording pressure-volume indicator diagrams on paper.
historical_context: Invented by James Watt's assistant John Southern to measure the internal power efficiency of rotative steam engines, powering the Industrial Revolution.
provenance: Retained in Boulton & Watt archives at Soho Foundry until 1895; acquired from Science Heritage collection, Birmingham, 1989.
restoration_notes: Surface oxidation stabilized; original pencil mechanism dry-lubricated with graphite. Trace diagram copy preserved alongside instrument.

name: Fragmentary Stele of the Neo-Babylonian Star Map and Zodiac
storage_location: Gallery A - Ancient Near East, Free-Standing Case 2
description: A dense basalt stone relief fragment carved with thirty celestial symbols, planetary constellations, and bilingual cuneiform star catalog entries.
historical_context: Dating to the reign of Nebuchadnezzar II; used by court astrologers (kalû) for astronomical diaries predicting lunar eclipses and royal omens.
provenance: Found near the Kasr mound in Babylon in 1913 by Robert Koldewey's team; dispersed during World War I; acquired in 1961.
restoration_notes: Structural basalt fracture consolidated with structural epoxy and internal stainless-steel armature in 1978. Monitored for surface micro-spalling.
